chunks: And Muhammad ibn Yaqub raised it, from al-Zuhri, who said:

I sought this matter (the Imam) with great effort until a good wealth of mine was spent on it, so I attached myself to al-Umari, served him, and stayed with him. After that, I asked him about the Master of the Age (peace be upon him). He said to me: 'There is no way for you to reach him.' I persisted, so he said to me: 'Come early in the morning.' I arrived, and he greeted me with a young man who was among the best of people in face and the most pleasant in scent, in the appearance of a merchant, and something was in his sleeve like the appearance of merchants. When I looked at him, I approached al-Umari, and he gestured to me. I turned to him and asked him, and he answered me about everything I wanted. Then he passed by to enter the house—which was one of the houses not much attended to—so al-Umari said: 'If you want to ask, ask, for you will not see him after this.' I went to ask, but he did not hear me, and he entered the house, and he did not speak to me more than saying: 'Accursed, accursed is the one who delays the 'Isha prayer until the stars become intertwined (close together). Accursed, accursed is the one who delays the Fajr (Morning) prayer until the stars disappear (fade away).' And he entered the house.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of delaying the 'Isha and Fajr prayers according to the Imam of the Age (a.s.)?
ai.summary: In this report from *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni narrates through al-Zuhri his arduous quest for the Hidden Imam, culminating in a fleeting encounter with al-Hasan ibn al-Walid (often identified as the Báb) who served as the Imam's gatekeeper. The Imam’s parting words highlight the spiritual peril of delaying the 'Isha prayer until the stars align and Fajr until they fade, a specific temporal marker emphasizing the importance of timely worship during the Occultation. This narration underscores the Shia belief in the continuous, albeit hidden, guidance of the Imam, who remains accessible to those who seek him with sincerity.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 236 - It is narrated from Muhammad bin Yaqub directly from Zuhri that he said:

“I made great efforts and spent a lot to meet Imam Mahdi (a.s). Thus I went to Amari and remained in his service. After a long time, I expressed to him the wish to see the Master of the Age (a.s). He said: There is no way you can meet him. When I continued to insist, he said: Come tomorrow at early dawn. So I came to him the next morning and found a young man in his company dressed as a trader and carrying some trading goods below his arms. I came near to Amari and he gestured to me. I moved towards that gentleman and asked him whatever I wanted. He replied and when he was about to go inside Amari said: If you want to ask him anything, ask him now; you will never see him again. As I was about to ask him something, he said the following and entered the room without listening to me: “Accursed, accursed is the one who delays the Maghrib Prayer so much that stars become visible. Accursed, accursed is the one who delays the Morning Prayer so much that stars disappear.”
